correctness.rationale: For odd n and char K coprime to n, the n Fourier modes w_a satisfy w_a*w_b=w_{-a} only if b=-2a. The Leibniz equation at every zero product forces all off-diagonal Fourier coefficients d_{x,a} to vanish, since its two possible nonzero output modes differ when b != -2a. Hence all derivations commute with the cyclic shift and are circulant over K. Substituting D(e_i)=sum_u c(u)e_{i+u} gives the exact iff coefficient relations c(0)=0, c(-u)=-c(u), c(u)=2c(2u). On additive-order-d classes the doubling-and-negation group <2,-1> acts freely with orbit size h_d, and the scalar multiplier is consistent precisely when p divides 2^t_d-1 and, if -1 is a doubling power, p divides 2^(t_d/2)+1. This yields the divisor-sum dimension formula and count q^dimension, with zero in char0 and char2. Direct derivation-matrix Leibniz kernels in n=3,5,7,9,11,13 over tested coprime primes match; n11 p3 and n13 p5 have dimension1. Explicit Legendre character convolution is compatible at n11 p3. This independently reconstructs the unrestricted proof.
residual_risks: Characteristic dividing n and even n explicitly excluded; Fourier-based proof requires semisimple roots of x^n-1.

originality.rationale: Elhamdadi–Makhlouf–Silvestrov–Zappala prove characteristic-zero odd-dihedral derivation vanishing and provide positive-characteristic computations for small quandle sizes (n up to 6). They do not give the all odd n, arbitrary coprime-positive-characteristic orbit resonance formula in the inspected complete text; their known char0 case is correctly credited. Aader’s thesis treats dihedral group-conjugation quandles with different underlying quandle, so no implication by title alone. The n11 p3 positive example and exact formula are nontrivial additions beyond small-case tables. Originality best of knowledge with literature-indexing risk.

value.rationale: The derivation Lie algebra is a fundamental invariant of a natural family of quandle algebras, and the exact all-order modular resonance formula is a motivated structure theorem. It exhibits a qualitatively new char-dependent jump from zero derivations to nonzero at the first n=11 p=3 example, and counts every derivation over finite fields. This goes beyond textbook character-zero vanishing or arbitrary small-n arithmetic.
